_meta.spec: CC Decision Engine - label rules (sibling of EMCA / OVCA labels.json; same record shape)
_meta.hard_rule: Every rule below was read from the retrieved label text via the DailyMed SPL v2 API (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/services/v2/spls/{setid}.xml). No rule was reconstructed from memory. Only Indications (§1, for indication wording), Dosage and Administration (§2) and Contraindications (§4) were read; Boxed Warnings and Warnings (§5) were not extracted for the new records.

_meta.on_label_warning: Of all agents in this file only TIVDAK (tisotumab vedotin) and KEYTRUDA (pembrolizumab) carry a cervical-cancer indication. TIVDAK §1: recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer with disease progression on or after chemotherapy. KEYTRUDA §1.12 (read 2026-10-06 from the same SPL the reused record cites, setid 9333c79b-d487-4538-a9f0-71b91a02b287, effectiveTime 20260710; the reused OVCA-era record itself does not quote it): with chemoradiotherapy for locally advanced CC FIGO 2014 stage III-IVA; with chemotherapy with or without bevacizumab for persistent, recurrent or metastatic CC with PD-L1 CPS >=1 by an FDA-authorized test; single agent for recurrent or metastatic CC with progression on or after chemotherapy and CPS >=1. LIBTAYO (cemiplimab) has no cervical indication in the US. The cytotoxics' cervical use is off-label unless their own reused record says otherwise, so their dose tables are for the labelled indications (NSCLC, breast, gastric, lymphoma etc.).
_meta.ctcae_version_warning: Label grade scales differ: LIBTAYO Table 2 uses CTCAE v4.0 (as do KEYTRUDA and TECENTRIQ); ALIMTA Table 1 uses NCI CTCAE v2; TIVDAK does not restate the version in §2; vinorelbine cites CTCAE without version; docetaxel §2.7 uses count thresholds and 'grade 3/4' without version; HYDREA, vincristine, MUTAMYCIN and MESNEX have no grade-based tables. Grade thresholds are copied as printed.
_meta.regimen_specific_warning: Docetaxel §2.7 is written per labelled regimen (breast single agent, TAC, NSCLC mono, docetaxel-cisplatin, prostate, TCF); rules carry the regimen in the 'ae' field. The TCF cisplatin/fluorouracil adjustment tables were not copied into the cisplatin / fluorouracil records.
_meta.field_note: Contraindications are stored as 'baseline_contraindications' (the field the ranker reads). 'label_indication' records §1 wording where on/off-label status matters for CC. The ranker matches /DISCONTINUE/i on 'action'; PERMANENTLY DISCONTINUE is written in capitals wherever the label says 'permanently discontinue', and lower-case 'discontinue' where the label does not say 'permanently' (docetaxel, vinorelbine, pemetrexed myelosuppression, mitomycin).
_meta.vault_scan: Regimen columns of CXCA_SquamousCell_Algorithm_v1.1.md and CXCA_AdenoCa_Algorithm_v1.1.md were scanned 2026-10-06; every systemic agent appearing in a regimen column has a key here. Olaparib and dostarlimab appear only in biomarker-definition rows (PAOLA-1 HRD cut-off, dMMR wording) and leucovorin only in a prior-therapy column, so they were not added. Radiotherapy and brachytherapy have no DailyMed label.

cisplatin.notes: IMPORTANT DIVERGENCE: the PLR label's §2.5 is three sentences with NO numeric thresholds. The older non-PLR generic label (CISPLATIN INJECTION [Hikma], setid 76aea034-6d58-4390-a164-36aa09c1f101, updated 2025-11-20) DOES carry numeric retreatment thresholds: repeat course withheld until serum creatinine <1.5 mg/100 mL and/or BUN <25 mg/100 mL; until platelets >=100,000/mm3 and WBC >=4,000/mm3; and until audiometry shows auditory acuity within normal limits. That older label also contraindicates pre-existing renal impairment, myelosuppression and hearing impairment. If the engine needs actionable numeric cisplatin thresholds they come only from the older-format label - version the two separately.

docetaxel.general_principle: §2.7 'Dosage Adjustments during Treatment' is written per labelled regimen; there is no single grade-based table. Rules below are transcribed per regimen; the single-agent (breast 60-100 mg/m2, NSCLC 75 mg/m2) blocks are the closest analogues to single-agent use in CC. §2.6: premedicate with oral corticosteroids (e.g. dexamethasone 16 mg/day for 3 days starting 1 day before) to reduce fluid retention and hypersensitivity. §2.2: 100 mg/m2 in previously treated NSCLC patients was associated with increased hematologic toxicity, infection and treatment-related mortality.
